- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply a “reversion buffer” — lower forecast by 1–3% in subsequent periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; apply a “horizon decay” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for the first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to “stick” to recent trend; apply a “sentiment smoothing” — average sentiment over 3–5 days before forecasting.
